string-array.name: faq_answers
string-array.item: "A: Mi Remote can control most devices that use an infrared remote, including TVs, ACs, and set-top boxes. It can't control devices that use Bluetooth or other wireless technologies instead of infrared, such as toy vehicles and some wireless lights."

"A: Phones with an infrared blaster can use Mi Remote's infrared controls. Other phones can generally use only Wi-Fi controls. Supported phones include Xiaomi 6, Xiaomi 5, Xiaomi 5s Plus, Xiaomi 5X, Xiaomi 5c, Xiaomi 4, Xiaomi 4C, Xiaomi 4S, Xiaomi Note 3, Xiaomi Note 2, Xiaomi Max 2, Xiaomi Max, REDMI Note 5, REDMI Note 4, REDMI Note 2, REDMI Note 3, REDMI 5 Plus, REDMI 5A, REDMI 5X, REDMI 4, REDMI 4A, REDMI 4X, and REDMI 3; Samsung Galaxy S3, S4, S5, S6, Note 2, Note 3, and Note 4; HONOR 6, HONOR 6 Plus, and HONOR 7; and the HTC One series."

A: The number of brands shown depends on your network connection. With a stable connection, Mi Remote loads the complete brand list online. If the connection is slow, it uses a smaller built-in infrared database instead. To view the complete list, go to Settings and turn on \"Use online data for new remotes\". The list may take longer to load on a slow connection.

A: The remote profile you selected may not match your AC. During setup, the second test button is used to turn off the AC. Follow the on-screen instructions and select \"Device responded\" only when the AC actually turns off. Then complete the setup again.

"A: First, check whether your TV remote uses infrared. Mi Remote can't control the TV if it uses another technology. If it uses infrared, select the correct TV brand and tap each test button several times to check whether the TV responds. When testing the power button, wait a little longer because some TVs take time to turn on."

A: Adding a set-top box adds its remote to Mi Remote. Once added, you can view its channel guide and program schedule on the \"TV programs\" page. You can also tap \"Switch channels\" in a program description to switch directly to that channel. Mi Remote supports both traditional and IPTV set-top boxes.
"A: You don't need to sign in to control devices or view TV listings. However, signing in with your Xiaomi Account is recommended."

"A: Your phone doesn't support infrared control, but it can control Xiaomi Boxes, Xiaomi TVs, and some standard Android smart TVs and boxes over Wi-Fi. If your phone and the device are connected to the same Wi-Fi but the device still isn't found, check your router settings and make sure AP isolation is turned off."

"A: Xiaomi Mi TV 3 series, Mi TV Bars, Mi Box 3 Enhanced Edition, and Mi Box Mini don't support infrared control. They can be controlled over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth instead. Connect your phone and TV to the same Wi-Fi and turn on the TV. Mi Remote should then find it automatically."
"A: Most lights use radio-frequency or other wireless controls instead of infrared, so they can't be controlled using Mi Remote."

"A: This message appears when Mi Remote doesn't have microphone permission. Allow microphone access in your phone's Settings > Permissions > App permissions > Mi Remote. After this, voice control should work normally."
